title: Products of ringed pro-etale open extensions without ambient quasi-compactness
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with restricted coefficient ring $R|_U$, via the slice identification [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Let $j_!$ be sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero module presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. For every family $(F_s)_{s\in S}$ of $R|_U$-module sheaves indexed by a set small in the fixed module universe, the canonical map
$$j_!\left(\prod_{s\in S}F_s\right)\longrightarrow\prod_{s\in S}j_!F_s,$$
whose $s$-th component is $j_!$ applied to the $s$-th projection, is an isomorphism of $R$-module sheaves, natural in maps of families. Products are the sectionwise limits of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. The empty family is included. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), kernel proof; module refinement with arbitrary ring sheaf, using the existing ringed recollement and closed-immersion limit nodes.

proof.text: Choose the reduced closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Put $L=j_!$, $J=j^{-1}$, $I=i^{-1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to $i,j,R$: it gives $\theta:JL\cong\mathrm{id}$, $IL=0$, exact $L,i_*$ and $0\to LJM\to M\to i_*IM\to0$ for every $M$. Only $j$ must be quasi-compact; no ambient qcqs clause is used.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), reduced closed complement; ringed localization input from lemma-ses-associated-to-open.

proof.text: Put $Q=\prod_sF_s$, $P=\prod_sLF_s$ and $c:LQ\to P$ with components $L(\mathrm{pr}_s)$. The products exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. Open restriction $J$ preserves them by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. Apply [lem-cbc-retraction-product-comparison] to $L,J,\theta$: its map $\beta$ has components $\theta_{F_s}J(\mathrm{pr}_s)$ and satisfies $\beta J(c)=\theta_Q$, so $J(c)$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), product comparison checked on the open; extracted retraction calculation.

proof.text: Closed restriction $I$ preserves products by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. Since $IL=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], one has $I(LQ)=0$ and $IP\cong\prod_sILF_s=0$. The last product is zero sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], including for an empty family. Thus $I(c)$ is a map between zero objects and is invertible.

If $JM=IM=0$, the short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] has zero outer terms, since exact $L,i_*$ preserve zero; hence $M=0$. The module categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $J,I$ preserve zero morphisms and finite limits and colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-pair-detects-isomorphisms] to $c$, using Steps 2 and 3: $c$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), detection using lemma-ses-associated-to-open; extracted exact-pair kernel/cokernel criterion.

proof.text: For a family map $(a_s:F_s\to G_s)_s$, both paths in the naturality square have $s$-th component $L(a_s\circ\mathrm{pr}_s)=L(a_s)\circ L(\mathrm{pr}_s)$. The product universal property proves equality; inverses are then natural too. For the empty family the sectionwise products are zero and exact $L$ preserves zero. These formulas also include $U=\varnothing$, $j=\mathrm{id}_X$, $X=\varnothing$ and the zero coefficient ring.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), canonical comparison; naturality and empty family by product uniqueness.
